item.title: Unit Circle Motion and the Sine and Cosine Graphs
item.stimulus: An angle of measure θ radians is drawn in standard position. Its terminal ray meets the unit circle centered at the origin at the point P. The functions f and g are defined by f(θ) = sin θ and g(θ) = cos θ for 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π. As θ increases, P moves counterclockwise around the unit circle, starting at (1, 0) when θ = 0. No calculator is permitted. Give exact values.
item.model_answer:
(a) At θ = π/2, P = (0, 1); at θ = π, P = (−1, 0). As θ increases from π/2 to π, P moves along the circle down toward the x-axis and to the left. f(θ) = sin θ is the y-coordinate of P, its vertical displacement from the x-axis, which decreases from 1 to 0, so f is decreasing on this interval. g(θ) = cos θ is the x-coordinate of P, its horizontal displacement from the y-axis, which decreases from 0 to −1, so g is also decreasing on this interval.

(b) The x-coordinate of a point on the unit circle is largest at (1, 0), where it equals 1. P is at (1, 0) when θ = 0 and when θ = 2π. So the maximum value of g is 1, at θ = 0 and θ = 2π. The y-coordinate is smallest at the lowest point (0, −1), where it equals −1. P is there only when θ = 3π/2. So the minimum value of f is −1, at θ = 3π/2.

(c) f increases when P moves up: from θ = 0 to π/2 and from θ = 3π/2 to 2π. g increases when P moves right: from θ = π to 2π. Both increase on 3π/2 ≤ θ ≤ 2π. On this interval P moves from (0, −1) to (1, 0): its vertical displacement from the x-axis rises from −1 to 0, so f increases, and its horizontal displacement from the y-axis rises from 0 to 1, so g increases. On 0 to π/2 the x-coordinate decreases, and on π to 3π/2 the y-coordinate decreases, so no other interval works.
item.verification_python:
import sympy as sp
th=sp.symbols('theta')
pi=sp.pi
# (a) endpoints
assert sp.sin(pi/2)==1 and sp.sin(pi)==0
assert sp.cos(pi/2)==0 and sp.cos(pi)==-1
import math
def incr(fn,a,b,n=200):
    xs=[a+(b-a)*k/n for k in range(n+1)]
    return all(fn(xs[i+1])>fn(xs[i]) for i in range(n))
def decr(fn,a,b,n=200):
    xs=[a+(b-a)*k/n for k in range(n+1)]
    return all(fn(xs[i+1])<fn(xs[i]) for i in range(n))
assert decr(math.sin,math.pi/2,math.pi)
assert decr(math.cos,math.pi/2,math.pi)
# (b)
assert sp.cos(0)==1 and sp.cos(2*pi)==1
sols=sp.solveset(sp.Eq(sp.cos(th),1),th,sp.Interval(0,2*pi))
assert sols==sp.FiniteSet(0,2*pi)
sols2=sp.solveset(sp.Eq(sp.sin(th),-1),th,sp.Interval(0,2*pi))
assert sols2==sp.FiniteSet(3*pi/2)
# (c)
assert incr(math.sin,3*math.pi/2,2*math.pi) and incr(math.cos,3*math.pi/2,2*math.pi)
assert sp.sin(3*pi/2)==-1 and sp.sin(2*pi)==0 and sp.cos(3*pi/2)==0 and sp.cos(2*pi)==1
# other quarters fail
assert not incr(math.cos,0,math.pi/2)
assert not incr(math.sin,math.pi/2,math.pi)
assert not incr(math.sin,math.pi,3*math.pi/2)
assert incr(math.sin,0,math.pi/2) and incr(math.cos,math.pi,2*math.pi)
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

parts.prompt: As θ increases from π/2 to π, decide whether f is increasing or decreasing and whether g is increasing or decreasing on that interval. Justify each answer by describing how the position of P changes.

criteria.text: States that f is decreasing on π/2 to π, justified by the vertical displacement of P from the x-axis decreasing from 1 to 0.
criteria.evidence: Says f is decreasing and explains that P moves from (0, 1) toward (−1, 0), so its y-coordinate (vertical displacement from the x-axis) drops from 1 to 0.
criteria.fix: Track the y-coordinate of P from (0, 1) to (−1, 0); sin θ equals that y-coordinate, so watch whether it rises or falls.
accepted_variants: f decreases because P moves down toward the x-axis
the y-coordinate of P goes from 1 to 0

criteria.text: States that g is decreasing on π/2 to π, justified by the x-coordinate of P going from 0 to −1 as P moves left of the y-axis.
criteria.evidence: Says g is decreasing and explains that P's x-coordinate (horizontal displacement from the y-axis) goes from 0 to −1 as P moves left.
criteria.fix: Remember cos θ is the x-coordinate of P; moving left on the circle makes the x-coordinate smaller, here from 0 to −1.
accepted_variants: g decreases because P moves to the left
the x-coordinate of P goes from 0 to −1

parts.prompt: Find the maximum value of g on 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π and every value of θ in that interval where it occurs. Then find the minimum value of f on 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π and every value of θ in that interval where it occurs. Give the location of P in each case.

criteria.text: Maximum value of g is 1, occurring at θ = 0 and θ = 2π, where P = (1, 0).
criteria.evidence: States maximum 1 and lists both θ = 0 and θ = 2π, identifying P at (1, 0), the point farthest right of the y-axis.
criteria.fix: Find the unit-circle point farthest right, (1, 0), and list every angle in 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π that lands there, including both endpoints.

criteria.text: Minimum value of f is −1, occurring only at θ = 3π/2, where P = (0, −1).
criteria.evidence: States minimum −1 at θ = 3π/2 with P at (0, −1), the lowest point on the unit circle.
criteria.fix: Find the lowest point of the unit circle, (0, −1); its y-coordinate is the minimum of sine, reached at θ = 3π/2.

parts.prompt: Find the interval of θ values in 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π on which f and g are both increasing. Explain your answer using the vertical and horizontal displacements of P.

criteria.text: Identifies the interval 3π/2 to 2π as the interval where both f and g are increasing.
criteria.evidence: Gives the interval from 3π/2 to 2π (open or closed endpoints both acceptable) and no other interval.
criteria.fix: List where sine increases (0 to π/2, 3π/2 to 2π) and where cosine increases (π to 2π), then take the overlap.

criteria.text: Justifies that on this interval P moves from (0, −1) to (1, 0), so its y-coordinate rises from −1 to 0 and its x-coordinate rises from 0 to 1.
criteria.evidence: Explains that in this quarter-turn P moves up (vertical displacement from the x-axis increases from −1 to 0) and right (horizontal displacement from the y-axis increases from 0 to 1), and notes that on other intervals at least one coordinate is not increasing.
criteria.fix: For each quarter-turn, record whether P moves up or down and left or right; both functions increase only when P moves up and right.
accepted_variants: P moves up and to the right from (0, −1) to (1, 0)
sin θ goes from −1 to 0 while cos θ goes from 0 to 1
